notes: How this part was researched: the session's web-search allowance was already spent when this part began (the one search asked was refused), so every page was reached directly, one request at a time, with the kit's honest User-Agent (states/net.py) and each site's robots.txt read first and obeyed: the campaign websites the candidates filed, each county's, city's, school district's and watershed district's own site, the Legislative Reference Library, the two state parties' sites and their local units' and caucuses' pages, the Green Party of Minnesota's site, the University of Minnesota's election archive, Wikipedia (one article), and four news organizations through their own site searches (KAXE, KAAL, Minnesota Lawyer, Southern Minnesota News). No search engine was read in place of the search tool. The page-reading tool was tried on four addresses that had failed or refused the script (the Senate District 47 DFL's site, two campaign addresses and the Belle Plaine district's site); it read nothing, because its address lookups failed or it met the same 404. The Senate District 47 DFL's site leaves two certificates out of its handshake; the reader fetched them from the addresses printed in the certificates themselves, as the kit's own repair does for one, and still required the chain to end at a root certifi trusts. The kit's reader, which follows one step only, may fail there.

The rule this part followed on robots.txt, stricter than the kit's own: stay out where a site turns away the kit's agent or Claude's reading agents by name, and also where it names AI assistants in general (it lists Anthropic's crawlers together with other makers' assistants). That kept this part out of the hometownsource.com papers (Star News of Elk River, Sun Post, ABC Newspapers, Morrison County Record), the Forum Communications papers (Brainerd Dispatch, Wadena Pioneer Journal, Post Bulletin, Worthington Globe), the Mankato Free Press, the Republican Eagle, Press Publications, the Aitkin Age, southernminn.com, KTTC, KEYC, MinnPost, the Pioneer Press and the Minnesota Reformer. Other parts cite hometownsource.com pages; whether that site's rule should be read this strictly is John's call. A site that names only Anthropic's training crawlers and leaves readers on a person's behalf alone was read: laurenforosseo.com (its campaign-site builder's standard robots.txt), KAAL, KSTP and Minnesota Lawyer. The kit's own fetch step checks robots.txt for the kit's agent only, so it will read laurenforosseo.com as well.

Not read, and nothing worked around: the Minnesota Judicial Branch's site and the state's mn.gov pages (not asked at all: other parts met a 403 and a CAPTCHA there), so neither judge has an official page and their offices rest on news reports; the City of Mankato's site (its robots.txt turns every unlisted script away), so Michael McLaughlin has no official page; the City of Minneapolis's boards and commissions system (403 to its robots.txt), so two appointed city seats rest on a campaign page and a party page; the Senate District 33 Republicans' site (403); the site searches of Olmsted County, Ramsey County, Crow Wing County and MPR News (robots.txt). The Belle Plaine school district's site did not answer on either day (connection timed out), the Stonewall DFL's site did not answer, and the Stevens County DFL's address shows an unrelated page in another language. The Star Tribune's robots.txt answered 429, so its rules could not be read and the site was left alone.

The campaign websites the candidates filed were learned by running the kit's own step (python -m ballot.local_sites files) on a scratch copy of the database; the real database was only read. Fifteen of this part's thirty candidates filed one, and each was opened. Thirteen are listed below. Two do not answer and are not listed: napierformayor.com (Dave Napier) has no address on the network today, and kamifornewbrighton.com (Kami Miller) answers 404 at every form of the address. Two that are listed arrive by a detour: Ethan Cha's www.ethanchamnhouse.com leads today to ethanchamnhouse.wordpress.com, and Jason Kalenborn's jason4edina.com does not answer over https and forwards over plain http to a Google Sites page. Carter Mc New's site is a single page drawn by script; its words were read in the script file the page loads (cartermcnew.com/assets/index-CqEVnJ4H.js). One more campaign site was found by asking whether a likely address exists and then reading it: Dawn Espe's espeforcrowwing.com, kept only because its own text names her, the office and 2026 (it is also drawn by script). Other likely addresses that exist were not campaign sites for these races and were dropped: workmanforcarvercounty.com (429 to the script, 404 to the reading tool), kellyforsheriff.com (no answer), castroforjudge.com (a parked-domain page).

For the second reader: (1) Julia Coleman and Ethan Cha are sitting members whose roster records have no birth date, so the Legislative Reference Library's is given, as parts 0, 1, 10 and 12 did. The Library marks Coleman's date "(uncertain)"; Wikipedia's article on her gives the same date. Only the year is recorded for her. (2) Tom Workman: the county's page says "First elected to Carver County Board in 2002"; the Library's record of him lists the county post as "2013 to ?". The county's own page is followed, and its election year is not turned into a start year. The Library gives his party as Independent Republican at his 1992 and 1994 elections and Republican at the three after, so there are two past_party entries, each in the Library's own word. (3) Jeffrey Veerkamp: the county's page gives only his latest election ("Elected: 2022"); the start year 2019 comes from the County Board's own synopses, which list Potter among the members present on December 18, 2018 and Veerkamp on January 8, 2019. The synopses give surnames only. (4) Travis J. Leiviska: the County Board's minutes of January 3, 2023 list the 2022 board without him and then record him sworn in that day. (5) Randy R Schreifels: the county's Auditor / Treasurer's Office page is drawn by script; the block headed with his name and the news items that call him Auditor-Treasurer are in the page's code, and a browser shows them. No page read says when he took office. (6) Matthew Westgaard, Kami Miller: the city pages list a "Matt Westgaard" and a "Kami Miller" on city bodies; no page read says in so many words that these are the candidates. The tie is the same name in the same city, on bodies of the government each is running to lead or join. Westgaard is not on the council today (the city's council page lists five other people); no page that could be read states any earlier service. (7) Carter Mc New: his campaign site and both government pages write the name McNew; a review item says so. His site's homeowners' association post is not a public office and is left out. (8) Michael McLaughlin: the one page found calls him Mike McLaughlin and does not name the ward; the tie is the name and the Mankato City Council, and nothing newer could be read, so no end is given. (9) Ruchi Gupta: the city's page names her chair of the Planning and Zoning Commission without years; the years are her campaign site's. (10) Hilary Birdsell: the district's page spells the name Hillary; a review item says so. Its Meet Our Board Members page is drawn by script and showed no text. (11) Leonardo Castro and Kimberly Wimmer: news reports only. Nothing read gives the day either took the bench, and nothing read from 2026 says in so many words that either sits today, so no end is given; each is the only candidate for the seat. (12) Kimberly Wimmer's school board seat is as of 2024; a judge would have had to give it up, but no page read says so. (13) Allyson Sellwood's campaign site says she served as a student trustee on "the board governing Minnesota's state colleges and universities" without years; the office is recorded in the site's own words. (14) Daniel Colten Schmidt's and Steven Young's seats on Minneapolis city advisory councils (the Green Zone Council, the Food Council) are appointed advisory posts without years; whether a card shows them is John's decision. Young's comes from the Green Party's page, so its kind is party, which the loader does not take for an office today. (15) Kari Dorry's 2022 run comes from the University's election archive, labelled secondary as parts 3 and 4 did; the birth date that archive shows was not taken, because the source it names is a birth records index. (16) The DFL Rural Caucus is a caucus of the state party; its page of 2026 endorsed candidates is recorded under endorsed_by for Dorry and Schmidt with the caucus named as the unit.

party_support (a key the loader does not read, in the shape parts 0, 6, 10 and 14 use): two listings where a party unit names a candidate without the word endorsed. The Carver County Republican Party's 2026 elections page shows a picture labelled "Tom Workman for Carver County Commissioner District 2" and the sentence "Tom Workman represents County Commissioner District 2" in its local section, under no heading that says endorsed or recommended; the 8th Congressional District Republicans list "HD 10A - Mark Striemer" on a page titled "2026 Candidates". They are kept apart from endorsed_by so that no page calls them endorsements; whether and how they are shown is John's decision. Mark Striemer's endorsement itself is recorded from the Aitkin County Republicans' page, which lists him among "MN GOP endorsed candidates" (the same list names the candidates the party's convention endorsed for statewide office, not the winners of the August primary). KAXE's headline on the primary result also calls him "endorsed Striemer" (https://www.kaxe.org/elections/2026-08-12/nathan-wesenberg-wins-primary-mark-striemer-advances).

Party pages read that name none of this part's candidates for nonpartisan offices: the Senate District 34 DFL (its letters of support for the Osseo school board went to three other candidates), the Senate District 37 DFL, the Senate District 50 DFL (its Edina letter of support went to other candidates), the Senate District 33, 30 and 36 DFL, the Senate District 35 Republicans (who recommend Jean Wayne's opponent in Coon Rapids Ward 3), the Senate District 37 Republicans' candidates page and the Senate District 50 Republicans' home page, the Kanabec, Crow Wing and Mille Lacs County Republicans, the Olmsted County Republicans' September newsletter, the Pope County DFL and the DFL Senior Caucus. Two campaign sites show endorsements as pictures only, which are not statements a card can quote: Kari Dorry's Endorsements page (logos of DFL caucuses; the Rural Caucus publishes its own list, which is recorded, and the Stonewall DFL's site did not answer) and Jean Wayne's post "Endorsements are coming in!".

Read and left out on purpose: ages given as "Age on Election Day" (KAXE's guides, for Bryan Savaloja and Scott Parsons), which do not fix a birth year; jobs, including posts in a sheriff's office and a county's emergency management, a county veterans service post, public defender work, legislative staff work and county staff work; military service; schools and graduation years; nonprofit, club and homeowners' association boards (among them the nonprofit boards Dawn Espe names in KAXE's guide); personal and labor endorsements; and everything campaign sites and the Library's records say of household, family and faith.

Nothing a card may show was found for Bryan Savaloja, Scott Parsons and Eric Johnson. Read for them: Wadena County's Sheriff page (the sheriff today is another person) and KAXE's stories and guide on the sheriff's race, which name no public office and no campaign website for Savaloja; the Brainerd district's Board of Education page (Parsons is not on the board) and KAXE's Brainerd School District guide, which names no public office he has held; for Eric Johnson, a common name, only the Belle Plaine district's own site could have tied anything to him, and it did not answer.

A slip to own up to: before the reader masked them, a few searches of raw page code printed contact addresses that pages publish (a party directory's unit contacts, two campaign sites' contact lines) into this part's working output. None was copied, stored or written into this file.
